notes: POC objective: validate Dedicated capacity for simulation prompt generation + chat support under production mix. Primary asks: throughput guarantees, p95 latency SLOs, reserved GPU planning, and contract SLA language.
Account background: standing platform vendor for AV simulation content; strong security posture, customer-facing assistants and scenario generation pipelines are latency-sensitive.
Key stakeholders: CTO (D. Hargrove) – product-led infra decisions, CISO (L. Moreno) – KMS/HSM + audit, Dir. ML Eng (S. Kato) – benchmarking owner.

Initial requirement summary: sustained throughput 400 reqs/sec (avg request = 64 tokens), burst to 1.2k reqs/sec for 5m windows, p95 generation latency <= 300ms for 64-token completions, endpoint failover between regions, data residency (NA) and VPC-only control plane.

Model preference: open-weights family (13B/70B) w/ quantized 4-bit for cost; evaluating both 13B and 70B variants for quality/latency tradeoffs. Routing: prefer low-latency primary (A) with cheaper fallback (B) when capacity constrained.
POC dates: environment stood up 2026-01-22; load test window 2026-01-26 to 2026-01-30; soak test scheduled 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-05 (72h continuous), can extend with signoff.
POC config notes: Dedicated pool = 8x A100-80GB equiv (initial), autoscale buffer +2 nodes for bursts, KV cache enabled for repeated prefixes, batching set to 32ms max latency budget.
Load test results (summary):
- 13B quantized baseline: sustained 420 reqs/sec at median latency 180ms (64-token), p95 = 290ms. CPU sidecar and networking overhead minimal.
- 70B quantized baseline: sustained 160 reqs/sec median 420ms, p95 = 690ms. Meets quality but not latency SLO without more GPUs or improved kernels.
- Burst behavior: with +2-node autoscale we saw 1.05k reqs/sec for 3-4 minutes before queueing; recommend increasing reserved burst capacity to +4 nodes or enable pre-warming for 5m windows.

Soak test findings (72h): throughput stable at target with 13B; observed KV cache hit-rate 23% for simulation prompts after warm-up; memory pressure within expected envelope; one transient 503 reported 2026-02-03 05:12 UTC (network flapping on host) — INF-4129 opened.
Representative prompts used (short samples):
- "Generate 8 diverse urban driving scenarios for rainy nighttime, include vehicle types and probable sensor occlusions" (avg 120 tokens output).
- "Assistant: summarize simulation result and recommend 3 parameter tunings to increase coverage" (avg 48 tokens).
- "Rank 100 candidate scenarios by failure-likelihood given prior logs" (reranking workload, batched scoring).

SLA negotiation points raised by Banyan: 24/7 incident bridge, credits for p95 breaches >3/day, guaranteed throughput floor during reserved window, KMS key rotation SLA, audit log retention 7 years (wants 10y option).

Redwood recommendations presented: reserve 12x A100-equivalent to meet p95 for 70B at target load, or adopt 13B primary + 70B fallback hybrid for cost balance. Suggested autoscale policy: baseline 8 nodes + burst +4 nodes with warm-up hooks for scheduled traffic spikes.
Cost sensitivity: finance asks for blended committed discount; current pricing estimate in drive deck, Banyan targeting <$0.02 / 1k tokens effective first-year after commit.
Quotes/commitments: CTO said 'if you can guarantee the p95 <300ms for our 13B mix with a clear path for 70B fallback we can sign a mid-Q1 commit' (paraphrase from 01/25 call).
